evidence: gpt-oss-120b: "# colour the graph (0/1)"; deepseek-v4-flash: "# BFS to color bipartite graph"; glm-5: "color" and component-based bipartitioning
affordance_in_statement: The transmitters in this network can be partitioned into two distinct operating frequencies. Every conflict pair always connects a transmitter on the first frequency to a transmitter on the second frequency
secondary_shortcut_name: truncate any sufficiently large independent set
removal_suggestion: There is no task-preserving way to remove this affordance because bipartiteness is the structural reason the exact problem is efficiently solvable. If changing the task is allowed, remove the promise that every conflict pair connects the two frequencies, making the conflict graph arbitrary.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the guaranteed bipartite structure to two-color the graph and then construct an independent set, likely via bipartite matching/vertex-cover machinery.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every conflict pair always connects a transmitter on the first frequency to a transmitter on the second frequency

common_affordance: The conflict graph is guaranteed to be bipartite because all conflicts cross the two operating frequencies.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It colors the graph, but its apparent color-class construction treats one bipartition side as sufficient for the optimum; a maximum independent set may mix the two sides, so coloring alone does not solve the exact problem.

Its special handling of m == 0 is valid, but the general approach relies on selecting a color group rather than computing a maximum independent set through bipartite matching/vertex cover; this misses larger mixed-side independent sets.

It independently colors connected components and compares their color groups, which still does not account for mixed-side independent sets within a component and therefore can underestimate the maximum size.

recommended_edit: If a single defeating edit is required, remove the explicit promise that conflict pairs cross two frequencies and state that the conflict graph is arbitrary. This defeats the bipartite-coloring/matching shortcut, although it changes the problem from a tractable structured problem to general maximum independent set.
